BiblicalUsage: Karar is to dance — to whirl, to spin round. David danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a linen ephod, while Michal watched from a window and despised him in her heart.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that David's dancing is worship without self-consciousness: he whirled before the ark and did not care who watched, and the one who despised him was the one left barren.
